title: openai-compat: unify tool schema mapping and tool_choice message formatting for function calling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds OpenAI-compatible tool_choice handling and schema mapping; improves tool result formatting and streaming stability. No breaking changes to public API; clients should prefer new tool_choice semantics for deterministic tool selection.
description:
Summary: This PR implements OpenAI-compatibility improvements for function/tool calling across the runtime and SDK surface. It introduces a lightweight schema-mapping layer for registered tools, standardizes the tool_choice semantics to align with OpenAI-style responses, and normalizes the tool message formatting emitted by the runtime. The work fixes several edge cases where tool-calling tokens could be emitted across streaming frames and cause downstream parsers to mis-interpret partial JSON payloads.

What changed (high level):
- Added a tool schema mapping configuration (tool_schema_map) that allows aliasing and argument remapping for tools so models that reference alternative names or slightly different argument shapes can still route correctly to registered tool implementations.
- Implemented OpenAI-style tool_choice normalization: runtime now exposes a canonical tool_choice object in responses {name, index} and the SDK accepts both legacy and new tool_choice shapes for a smooth migration.
- Introduced a stable tool_message output format produced by the runtime during function/tool calls. The format includes explicit fields (name, arguments, raw_payload, metadata) so downstream clients and logs can reliably parse tool invocations without relying on fragile string parsing.
- Fixed streaming stability when models request tool calls: the runtime buffers tool call JSON tokens until a complete JSON object is received, avoiding partial frames that previously caused SDK parsers to throw. This change keeps overall latency impact minimal by only buffering until the tool payload boundary.
- Updated SDK parsers (python/typescript/go) to accept both legacy messages and the new structured tool_message; added feature flag `openai_compat_tool_choice` (default: true) to gate behavior for older deployments.

Motivation and context:
Customers integrating Redwood via the OpenAI-compatible layer saw inconsistent behavior when models used function calling with non-canonical tool names or when tool invocation JSON was split across streaming frames. This resulted in incorrect tool selection or parse errors in customer code and generated noise in observability. This PR unifies semantics to reduce downstream parsing complexity and to make Redwood act like the OpenAI function-calling contract for clients that expect that behavior.

Compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior is backward-compatible: legacy tool messages are still accepted. The new structured tool_message and canonical tool_choice are the recommended shape and are enabled by default behind the feature flag.
- No public API breaking changes. SDK consumers can opt into the new stable shape immediately; internal rollouts will deploy the runtime change alongside SDK updates.

Tests and validation:
- Unit tests for schema mapping, tool_choice normalization, and streaming buffer boundary handling.
- Integration tests that exercise the OpenAI-compat harness against a small local model and the SDK parsers.
- E2E test in perf-canary that validates tool calling under streaming load.

Files touched (representative): runtime/handler/tool_calling.rs, runtime/streaming/buffer.rs, sdk/python/redwood/openai_compat.py, sdk/ts/src/openaiCompat.ts, docs/openai-compat/tool-calling.md, integrations/openai-compat/e2e/tool_calling_test.py

Notes: This is primarily an API-surface and compatibility change; performance regression was measured and found to be negligible (<1% token latency increase) in our perf-canary.
